questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: Had I known about the delay, I would have taken a later train.
options.B: If I would have known about the delay, I would have taken a later train.
options.C: Had I known about the delay, I would take a later train.
options.D: If I had known about the delay, I would have taken a later train.

name.en: Third Conditional and Its Inverted Form
name.id: Kondisional Tipe Ketiga dan Bentuk Inversinya

details_explanation.explanation: Both A and D are correct third-conditional sentences. A uses inversion ('Had I known' = 'If I had known'), and D uses the full 'if' clause. B wrongly puts 'would have' in the if-clause, and C mixes a past condition with a present result.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the third conditional, which describes an unreal past situation and its imagined past result. The structure is 'If + past perfect, subject + would have + past participle'. In formal English, 'if' can be dropped and 'had' moved before the subject: 'Had I known...'.

rules.title: 1. Standard Third Conditional
rules.explanation: Use the past perfect in the if-clause and 'would have + past participle' in the result clause.
rules.structure: If + had + past participle, subject + would have + past participle.
notes: Correct: If I had known, I would have taken a later train.
Incorrect: If I would have known, I would have taken a later train.

rules.title: 2. Inverted Third Conditional
rules.explanation: Drop 'if' and place 'had' before the subject. The meaning stays the same.
rules.structure: Had + subject + past participle, subject + would have + past participle.
notes: Correct: Had I known, I would have taken a later train.
Do not write: If had I known...

rules.title: 3. Why C Is Wrong
rules.explanation: Option C uses 'would take' (a present/future unreal result) with a past unreal condition. This is an inconsistent mix.
rules.structure: Past condition → past result ('would have taken').
notes: Correct answers: A and D.
C would only work if the result were also present: 'If I had taken the earlier train, I would be there now.'

common_mistakes.wrong: If I would have known, I would have told you.
common_mistakes.correct: If I had known, I would have told you. / Had I known, I would have told you.
common_mistakes.reason: Never use 'would have' in the if-clause of a third conditional.

common_mistakes.wrong: Had I would have known, I would have told you.
common_mistakes.correct: Had I known, I would have told you.
common_mistakes.reason: After inverted 'Had', use the past participle only.

other_examples.sentence: Had she applied earlier, she would have been accepted.
other_examples.translation: Jika saja dia melamar lebih awal, dia akan telah diterima.

explanation.en: Inverted third conditional with 'Had she applied'.
explanation.id: Kondisional tipe ketiga inversi dengan 'Had she applied'.

other_examples.sentence: If they had booked the tickets in advance, they would have paid less.
other_examples.translation: Jika saja mereka memesan tiket lebih awal, mereka akan telah membayar lebih sedikit.

explanation.en: Standard third conditional with past perfect and 'would have paid'.
explanation.id: Kondisional tipe ketiga standar dengan past perfect dan 'would have paid'.

other_examples.sentence: Had we not missed the exit, we would have arrived on time.
other_examples.translation: Jika saja kami tidak melewatkan jalan keluar, kami akan telah tiba tepat waktu.

explanation.en: Negative inversion: 'Had we not missed' = 'If we had not missed'.
explanation.id: Inversi negatif: 'Had we not missed' = 'If we had not missed'.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: Never have I seen such a spectacular performance.
options.B: Never I have seen such a spectacular performance.
options.C: Rarely does she complain about the workload.
options.D: Rarely she complains about the workload.

details_explanation.explanation: When a negative or limiting adverbial such as 'never', 'rarely', 'seldom', or 'hardly' starts a sentence, the auxiliary verb comes before the subject. A and C follow this rule; B and D keep normal word order.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests subject–auxiliary inversion after negative adverbials placed at the beginning of a sentence for emphasis. This is a formal, high-level structure common in C1/C2 writing.

rules.title: 1. Negative Adverbial + Auxiliary + Subject
rules.explanation: Move the auxiliary (have, do, is, can, etc.) before the subject after a fronted negative adverbial.
rules.structure: Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject + main verb.
notes: Correct: Never have I seen...
Incorrect: Never I have seen...

rules.title: 2. Present Simple Needs 'do/does'
rules.explanation: If there is no auxiliary, insert 'do/does/did'.
rules.structure: Rarely + does + subject + base verb.
notes: Correct: Rarely does she complain.
Incorrect: Rarely she complains.

rules.title: 3. Common Triggers
rules.explanation: Typical triggers: never, rarely, seldom, hardly, scarcely, no sooner, not only, little, under no circumstances.
rules.structure: Trigger + auxiliary + subject + verb.
notes: Correct answers: A and C.
These structures are emphatic and mostly formal.

common_mistakes.wrong: Seldom he goes to the cinema.
common_mistakes.correct: Seldom does he go to the cinema.
common_mistakes.reason: Fronted negative adverbials require inversion with 'do/does/did'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Hardly I had arrived when the phone rang.
common_mistakes.correct: Hardly had I arrived when the phone rang.
common_mistakes.reason: Use inversion after 'hardly'.

other_examples.sentence: Seldom have we witnessed such dedication.
other_examples.translation: Jarang sekali kami menyaksikan dedikasi seperti itu.

explanation.en: 'Seldom' triggers inversion with 'have'.
explanation.id: 'Seldom' memicu inversi dengan 'have'.

other_examples.sentence: Not only did she finish first, but she also broke the record.
other_examples.translation: Tidak hanya dia finis pertama, tetapi dia juga memecahkan rekor.

explanation.en: 'Not only' at the start requires inversion with 'did'.
explanation.id: 'Not only' di awal memerlukan inversi dengan 'did'.

other_examples.sentence: Under no circumstances should you share this password.
other_examples.translation: Dalam keadaan apa pun kamu tidak boleh membagikan kata sandi ini.

explanation.en: A fronted negative phrase forces 'should' before the subject.
explanation.id: Frasa negatif di awal memaksa 'should' mendahului subjek.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: The board insisted that the report be submitted by Friday.
options.B: The board insisted that the report is submitted by Friday.
options.C: The board insisted that the report should be submitted by Friday.
options.D: The board insisted that the report was be submitted by Friday.

details_explanation.explanation: After 'insist that', English uses either the base-form subjunctive ('be submitted') or 'should + base form' ('should be submitted'). A and C are both correct. B uses the wrong tense, and D is ungrammatical.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the mandative subjunctive used after verbs such as insist, demand, request, recommend, and suggest. American English strongly prefers the base form; British English often accepts 'should + base form'.

rules.title: 1. Base-Form Subjunctive
rules.explanation: Use the base form of the verb after 'insist that + subject', even with third-person singular subjects.
rules.structure: insist that + subject + base verb.
notes: Correct: insisted that the report be submitted.
Incorrect: insisted that the report is submitted.

rules.title: 2. 'Should' Alternative
rules.explanation: In British English, 'should + base verb' is also acceptable after these verbs.
rules.structure: insist that + subject + should + base verb.
notes: Correct: insisted that the report should be submitted.
Both forms carry the same meaning.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: B uses the present indicative, which does not express the demanded action. D combines 'was' and 'be', which is never grammatical.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Related verbs: demand, request, recommend, propose, urge.
After 'It is essential/important that...', the same subjunctive is used.

common_mistakes.wrong: She demanded that he leaves immediately.
common_mistakes.correct: She demanded that he leave immediately.
common_mistakes.reason: Use the base form in the mandative subjunctive.

common_mistakes.wrong: It is vital that every student is informed.
common_mistakes.correct: It is vital that every student be informed.
common_mistakes.reason: The subjunctive base form is used after 'it is vital that'.

other_examples.sentence: The doctor recommended that he rest for a week.
other_examples.translation: Dokter menyarankan agar dia beristirahat selama seminggu.

explanation.en: Base form 'rest' after 'recommended that'.
explanation.id: Bentuk dasar 'rest' setelah 'recommended that'.

other_examples.sentence: It is essential that all applicants be interviewed in person.
other_examples.translation: Penting bahwa semua pelamar diwawancarai secara langsung.

explanation.en: Subjunctive 'be' after 'It is essential that'.
explanation.id: Subjungtif 'be' setelah 'It is essential that'.

other_examples.sentence: They requested that the meeting should be postponed.
other_examples.translation: Mereka meminta agar rapat ditunda.

explanation.en: British English allows 'should + base form'.
explanation.id: Bahasa Inggris Britania membolehkan 'should + bentuk dasar'.

questions.question: Which TWO options correctly complete the sentence? 'The manuscript ___ before the editor arrived.'

details_explanation.explanation: The manuscript is the receiver of the action, so the passive is needed: 'should have been proofread' and 'ought to have been proofread' are both correct. B and D are active forms, which would mean the manuscript proofread something.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the passive form of modal perfect structures. The pattern is 'modal + have been + past participle' when the subject receives the action and the criticism or expectation refers to the past.

rules.title: 1. Passive Modal Perfect Structure
rules.explanation: Use 'modal + have been + past participle' for a past action done to the subject.
rules.structure: Subject + modal + have been + past participle.
notes: Correct: should have been proofread.
Correct: ought to have been proofread.

rules.title: 2. Active vs Passive
rules.explanation: If the subject performs the action, use the active: 'should have proofread'. If the subject receives it, use the passive.
rules.structure: Active: should have + past participle. Passive: should have been + past participle.
notes: The manuscript cannot proofread itself.
'Ought to' follows the same pattern as 'should'.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: B ('must have proofread') is active and expresses a deduction, not criticism of an unfulfilled duty. D ('should have proofread') is also active.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Related forms: could have been, might have been, needn't have been.

common_mistakes.wrong: The report should have submitted yesterday.
common_mistakes.correct: The report should have been submitted yesterday.
common_mistakes.reason: The report receives the action, so the passive is required.

common_mistakes.wrong: The forms ought to been signed.
common_mistakes.correct: The forms ought to have been signed.
common_mistakes.reason: Keep 'have been' after 'ought to'.

other_examples.sentence: The invoice should have been paid last week.
other_examples.translation: Faktur itu seharusnya sudah dibayar minggu lalu.

explanation.en: Passive modal perfect: the invoice receives the action.
explanation.id: Modal perfect pasif: faktur menerima tindakan.

other_examples.sentence: The windows ought to have been cleaned before the guests arrived.
other_examples.translation: Jendela-jendela seharusnya sudah dibersihkan sebelum tamu datang.

explanation.en: 'Ought to have been + past participle' for an unfulfilled obligation.
explanation.id: 'Ought to have been + past participle' untuk kewajiban yang tidak terpenuhi.

other_examples.sentence: The results could have been announced earlier.
other_examples.translation: Hasilnya bisa saja diumumkan lebih awal.

explanation.en: 'Could have been announced' is a passive modal perfect.
explanation.id: 'Could have been announced' adalah modal perfect pasif.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: It was in Jakarta that they first met.
options.B: It was in Jakarta where they first met.
options.C: What I need is a good night's sleep.
options.D: What I need it is a good night's sleep.

details_explanation.explanation: A is a correct 'it'-cleft ('It was in Jakarta that...'), and C is a correct 'wh'-cleft ('What I need is...'). B wrongly uses 'where' instead of 'that', and D repeats the object with 'it'.
details_explanation.introduction: Cleft sentences split one idea into two clauses to emphasise a particular piece of information. This structure is very common in C1/C2 writing and speaking.

rules.title: 1. 'It'-Cleft
rules.explanation: Use 'It + be + emphasised part + that/who + rest of clause'.
rules.structure: It was + [emphasis] + that + subject + verb.
notes: Correct: It was in Jakarta that they first met.
Use 'who' for people: It was Maria who called.

rules.title: 2. 'Wh'-Cleft
rules.explanation: Use 'What + subject + verb + be + emphasised part'.
rules.structure: What + clause + be + noun phrase.
notes: Correct: What I need is a good night's sleep.
Do not add an extra 'it'.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: B uses 'where' after 'It was in Jakarta', which mixes a relative clause with a cleft. D repeats the object with 'it' after 'What I need'.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Clefts do not change meaning; they only add emphasis.

common_mistakes.wrong: It was my brother which broke the window.
common_mistakes.correct: It was my brother who broke the window.
common_mistakes.reason: Use 'who' for people in an 'it'-cleft.

common_mistakes.wrong: What she wants it is a new phone.
common_mistakes.correct: What she wants is a new phone.
common_mistakes.reason: Do not repeat the object after 'what'.

other_examples.sentence: It was the manager who approved the request.
other_examples.translation: Manajerlah yang menyetujui permintaan itu.

explanation.en: 'Who' is used for a person in an 'it'-cleft.
explanation.id: 'Who' digunakan untuk orang dalam 'it'-cleft.

other_examples.sentence: What surprised me was his calm reaction.
other_examples.translation: Yang mengejutkan saya adalah reaksinya yang tenang.

explanation.en: A 'wh'-cleft with 'What surprised me'.
explanation.id: 'Wh'-cleft dengan 'What surprised me'.

other_examples.sentence: It was not until midnight that he finally arrived.
other_examples.translation: Baru pada tengah malam dia akhirnya tiba.

explanation.en: A negative 'it'-cleft with 'not until'.
explanation.id: 'It'-cleft negatif dengan 'not until'.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: She remembered locking the door before she left.
options.B: She remembered to lock the door before she left.
options.C: She remembered lock the door before she left.
options.D: She remembered to locking the door before she left.

details_explanation.explanation: Both A and B are correct but with different meanings. 'Remember + gerund' means recalling a past action; 'remember + to-infinitive' means not forgetting to do a future action.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests verbs that change meaning depending on whether they are followed by a gerund or an infinitive. 'Remember' is a classic example, along with 'stop', 'regret', and 'try'.

rules.title: 1. Remember + Gerund
rules.explanation: This means you have a memory of doing something in the past.
rules.structure: remember + verb-ing.
notes: Correct: She remembered locking the door. (She recalled doing it.)
The action happened before the remembering.

rules.title: 2. Remember + To-Infinitive
rules.explanation: This means you did not forget to do a necessary action.
rules.structure: remember + to + base verb.
notes: Correct: She remembered to lock the door. (She did not forget.)
The action happens at or after the remembering.

rules.title: 3. Why C and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: C uses the bare base form after 'remembered', which is ungrammatical. D mixes 'to' with a gerund.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and B.
notes: Both A and B are grammatical; only the meaning differs.

common_mistakes.wrong: I remember to meet him at the airport last year.
common_mistakes.correct: I remember meeting him at the airport last year.
common_mistakes.reason: Use the gerund for a past memory.

common_mistakes.wrong: Please remember locking the door when you leave.
common_mistakes.correct: Please remember to lock the door when you leave.
common_mistakes.reason: Use the infinitive for a future obligation.

other_examples.sentence: He stopped smoking last year.
other_examples.translation: Dia berhenti merokok tahun lalu.

explanation.en: 'Stop + gerund' means to quit an activity.
explanation.id: 'Stop + gerund' berarti berhenti dari suatu aktivitas.

other_examples.sentence: He stopped to smoke a cigarette.
other_examples.translation: Dia berhenti untuk merokok sebatang.

explanation.en: 'Stop + infinitive' means to pause in order to do something.
explanation.id: 'Stop + infinitive' berarti berhenti sejenak untuk melakukan sesuatu.

other_examples.sentence: I regret telling her the truth.
other_examples.translation: Saya menyesal telah mengatakan kebenaran kepadanya.

explanation.en: 'Regret + gerund' refers to a past action you wish you had not done.
explanation.id: 'Regret + gerund' merujuk pada tindakan lampau yang disesali.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: Having finished the report, she sent it to her manager.
options.B: Finished the report, she sent it to her manager.
options.C: The report having been finished, she sent it to her manager.
options.D: The report finishing, she sent it to her manager.

details_explanation.explanation: A uses a perfect active participle ('Having finished') and C uses an absolute construction with a passive perfect participle ('The report having been finished'). Both are correct. B lacks 'having', and D uses an active participle with a passive meaning.
details_explanation.introduction: Participle clauses replace full clauses to make writing more concise. This is a C1/C2 structure that appears frequently in academic and formal writing.

rules.title: 1. Perfect Participle for Earlier Actions
rules.explanation: Use 'Having + past participle' when the participle action happened before the main verb.
rules.structure: Having + past participle, main clause.
notes: Correct: Having finished the report, she sent it...
The subject of both clauses must be the same.

rules.title: 2. Absolute Construction
rules.explanation: A noun + participle can form an independent structure. The passive form is 'noun + having been + past participle'.
rules.structure: Noun + having been + past participle, main clause.
notes: Correct: The report having been finished, she sent it...
This structure is common in formal writing.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: B uses 'Finished' without 'having', which sounds like the subject was finished. D uses active 'finishing', but the report does not finish anything.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Check that the participle matches the meaning (active or passive).

common_mistakes.wrong: Walking down the street, the rain started.
common_mistakes.correct: Walking down the street, I felt the rain start.
common_mistakes.reason: The participle subject must match the main clause subject.

common_mistakes.wrong: Being finished the work, he left.
common_mistakes.correct: Having finished the work, he left.
common_mistakes.reason: Use 'having + past participle' for an earlier action.

other_examples.sentence: Having read the instructions, he assembled the furniture easily.
other_examples.translation: Setelah membaca instruksinya, dia merakit furnitur itu dengan mudah.

explanation.en: 'Having read' shows the reading happened first.
explanation.id: 'Having read' menunjukkan membaca terjadi lebih dulu.

other_examples.sentence: The meeting having ended, everyone went home.
other_examples.translation: Setelah rapat berakhir, semua orang pulang.

explanation.en: An absolute construction with 'having ended'.
explanation.id: Konstruksi absolut dengan 'having ended'.

other_examples.sentence: Not knowing the answer, she kept silent.
other_examples.translation: Karena tidak tahu jawabannya, dia tetap diam.

explanation.en: Present participle for a simultaneous state.
explanation.id: Partisip present untuk keadaan yang bersamaan.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: She asked me where I had been the previous night.
options.B: She asked me where had I been the previous night.
options.C: She wondered whether he would accept the offer.
options.D: She wondered whether would he accept the offer.

details_explanation.explanation: In reported questions, the word order is statement order (subject before verb), with no auxiliary inversion and no question mark. A and C follow this rule; B and D keep question order.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests reported questions, which are common in C1 exams. Whether the question is a wh-question or a yes/no question, the reported clause uses normal statement word order.

rules.title: 1. Statement Word Order
rules.explanation: After the reporting verb, put the subject before the verb; do not invert.
rules.structure: asked + question word + subject + verb.
notes: Correct: asked me where I had been.
Incorrect: asked me where had I been.

rules.title: 2. Yes/No Questions Use 'if' or 'whether'
rules.explanation: For yes/no questions, use 'if' or 'whether' and statement order.
rules.structure: wondered whether + subject + verb.
notes: Correct: wondered whether he would accept.
Incorrect: wondered whether would he accept.

rules.title: 3. Tense Backshift
rules.explanation: When the reporting verb is past, shift the reported verb back: 'are' → 'were', 'will' → 'would', 'have been' → 'had been'.
rules.structure: asked + where + subject + had been.
notes: Correct answers: A and C.
No question mark is used in reported questions.

common_mistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
common_mistakes.correct: He asked me where I lived.
common_mistakes.reason: Reported questions use statement order.

common_mistakes.wrong: She asked if was I ready.
common_mistakes.correct: She asked if I was ready.
common_mistakes.reason: Do not invert after 'if' in reported speech.

other_examples.sentence: The interviewer asked how long I had worked in sales.
other_examples.translation: Pewawancara bertanya berapa lama saya bekerja di bidang penjualan.

explanation.en: Statement order with backshift 'had worked'.
explanation.id: Urutan pernyataan dengan backshift 'had worked'.

other_examples.sentence: He wanted to know whether the shop was still open.
other_examples.translation: Dia ingin tahu apakah tokonya masih buka.

explanation.en: 'Whether' introduces a reported yes/no question.
explanation.id: 'Whether' memperkenalkan pertanyaan yes/no tak langsung.

other_examples.sentence: They asked what time the train left.
other_examples.translation: Mereka bertanya pukul berapa keretanya berangkat.

explanation.en: 'What time the train left' uses statement order.
explanation.id: 'What time the train left' menggunakan urutan pernyataan.

questions.question: Which TWO options correctly complete the sentence? '___ hard he tried, he could not solve the puzzle.'

details_explanation.explanation: 'However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb' and 'No matter how + adjective/adverb + subject + verb' are both correct concessive structures. 'Whatever' needs a noun, and 'Although' needs a full clause without inversion.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests advanced concessive linkers. 'However' and 'no matter how' are followed by an adjective or adverb, then the subject and verb — with no 'that' and no inversion of the main clause.

rules.title: 1. However + Adjective/Adverb
rules.explanation: 'However' here means 'to whatever degree' and is followed by an adjective or adverb.
rules.structure: However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb, main clause.
notes: Correct: However hard he tried...
Do not confuse with sentence-initial 'However,' meaning 'nevertheless'.

rules.title: 2. No Matter How
rules.explanation: 'No matter how' has the same meaning and the same word order.
rules.structure: No matter how + adjective/adverb + subject + verb, main clause.
notes: Correct: No matter how hard he tried...
'No matter what' takes a noun or clause instead.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: 'Whatever' cannot be followed by an adjective + clause here. 'Although' needs a complete clause: 'Although he tried hard, ...'.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Related forms: whoever, wherever, whenever, whichever.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although hard he tried, he failed.
common_mistakes.correct: However hard he tried, he failed. / Although he tried hard, he failed.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Although' needs a full clause with subject + verb.

common_mistakes.wrong: Whatever hard he tried, he failed.
common_mistakes.correct: However hard he tried, he failed.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Whatever' does not take an adjective + clause.

other_examples.sentence: However carefully she explained, nobody understood.
other_examples.translation: Betapa pun hati-hati dia menjelaskan, tidak ada yang mengerti.

explanation.en: 'However + adverb + clause' shows concession.
explanation.id: 'However + adverb + klausa' menunjukkan konsesi.

other_examples.sentence: No matter how expensive it is, I will buy it.
other_examples.translation: Betapa pun mahalnya, saya akan membelinya.

explanation.en: 'No matter how' works the same as concessive 'however'.
explanation.id: 'No matter how' berfungsi sama dengan 'however' konsesif.

other_examples.sentence: Whatever you decide, I will support you.
other_examples.translation: Apa pun yang kamu putuskan, saya akan mendukungmu.

explanation.en: 'Whatever' is used when a noun or clause follows.
explanation.id: 'Whatever' digunakan ketika diikuti nomina atau klausa.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: The information you gave me was extremely useful.
options.B: The informations you gave me were extremely useful.
options.C: He gave me some useful advice.
options.D: He gave me some useful advices.

details_explanation.explanation: 'Information' and 'advice' are uncountable in English. They have no plural form and take singular verbs. A and C are correct; B and D incorrectly add '-s'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests uncountable nouns that are commonly miscounted by Indonesian learners, such as information, advice, furniture, equipment, luggage, and news.

rules.title: 1. No Plural Form
rules.explanation: Uncountable nouns do not take '-s' and are not used with 'a/an'.
rules.structure: some information / a piece of information.
notes: Correct: some advice.
Incorrect: some advices.

rules.title: 2. Singular Verb Agreement
rules.explanation: Uncountable nouns take singular verbs.
rules.structure: The information + is/was.
notes: Correct: The information was useful.
Incorrect: The informations were useful.

rules.title: 3. Counting with Partitives
rules.explanation: To count uncountable nouns, use a partitive such as 'a piece of', 'an item of', or 'a bit of'.
rules.structure: a piece of advice / two pieces of furniture.
notes: Correct answers: A and C.
Other uncountables: research, evidence, machinery, staff (often).

common_mistakes.wrong: She gave me two advices.
common_mistakes.correct: She gave me two pieces of advice.
common_mistakes.reason: Use a partitive to count uncountable nouns.

common_mistakes.wrong: The furnitures are new.
common_mistakes.correct: The furniture is new.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Furniture' is uncountable and singular.

other_examples.sentence: The equipment in the lab is outdated.
other_examples.translation: Peralatan di laboratorium itu sudah usang.

explanation.en: 'Equipment' is uncountable and takes 'is'.
explanation.id: 'Equipment' tidak terhitung dan menggunakan 'is'.

other_examples.sentence: She gave me a useful piece of advice.
other_examples.translation: Dia memberi saya sepotong nasihat yang berguna.

explanation.en: 'A piece of advice' counts an uncountable noun.
explanation.id: 'A piece of advice' menghitung kata benda tak terhitung.

other_examples.sentence: The research on renewable energy is promising.
other_examples.translation: Penelitian tentang energi terbarukan itu menjanjikan.

explanation.en: 'Research' is uncountable and singular.
explanation.id: 'Research' tidak terhitung dan tunggal.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: So difficult was the exam that many students failed.
options.B: So difficult the exam was that many students failed.
options.C: Such was his anger that he could not speak.
options.D: Such his anger was that he could not speak.

details_explanation.explanation: With 'So + adjective + be + subject + that...' and 'Such + be + noun phrase + that...', the verb comes before the subject. A and C follow this pattern; B and D keep normal order after the fronted phrase.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests emphatic inversion with 'so ... that' and 'such ... that'. These structures are common in formal and literary English, especially at C1/C2 level.

rules.title: 1. 'So + Adjective' Inversion
rules.explanation: When 'so + adjective' starts the sentence, invert the subject and 'be'.
rules.structure: So + adjective + be + subject + that + clause.
notes: Correct: So difficult was the exam that...
This emphasises the degree of the adjective.

rules.title: 2. 'Such + Noun' Inversion
rules.explanation: 'Such' can start the sentence with a noun phrase, followed by inversion of 'be'.
rules.structure: Such + be + noun phrase + that + clause.
notes: Correct: Such was his anger that...
Such + (a/an) + adjective + noun is also possible.

rules.title: 3. Why B and D Are Wrong
rules.explanation: B and D keep normal subject–verb order after the fronted 'so/such'. Inversion is required when the phrase is moved to the front.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: A non-inverted version is also correct: The exam was so difficult that many students failed.

common_mistakes.wrong: So tired he was that he fell asleep.
common_mistakes.correct: So tired was he that he fell asleep.
common_mistakes.reason: Invert subject and verb after fronted 'so + adjective'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Such was his kindness he helped everyone.
common_mistakes.correct: Such was his kindness that he helped everyone.
common_mistakes.reason: Keep 'that' in the result clause.

other_examples.sentence: So loudly did she shout that everyone turned around.
other_examples.translation: Begitu keras dia berteriak sehingga semua orang menoleh.

explanation.en: 'So + adverb' with inversion using 'did'.
explanation.id: 'So + adverb' dengan inversi menggunakan 'did'.

other_examples.sentence: Such was the demand that tickets sold out in minutes.
other_examples.translation: Begitu besar permintaannya sehingga tiket habis dalam hitungan menit.

explanation.en: 'Such was + noun phrase' with inversion.
explanation.id: 'Such was + frasa nomina' dengan inversi.

other_examples.sentence: So convincing was his argument that nobody objected.
other_examples.translation: Begitu meyakinkan argumennya sehingga tidak ada yang membantah.

explanation.en: Inversion after 'so + adjective'.
explanation.id: Inversi setelah 'so + adjective'.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following sentences are grammatically correct?

options.A: I wish I had studied harder for the exam.
options.B: I wish I have studied harder for the exam.
options.C: If only she would listen to me.
options.D: If only she will listen to me.

details_explanation.explanation: 'Wish + past perfect' expresses regret about the past, so A is correct. 'If only + would' expresses a wish for change, so C is correct. B uses a present perfect after 'wish', and D uses 'will' instead of 'would'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests hypothetical wishes. 'Wish' and 'if only' take past forms to express unreal situations: past simple for present wishes, past perfect for past regrets, and 'would' for wishes about other people's behaviour.

rules.title: 1. Wish + Past Simple (Present Regret)
rules.explanation: Use the past simple to express a wish about the present.
rules.structure: wish + subject + past simple.
notes: Correct: I wish I knew the answer.
'Were' is used instead of 'was' in formal English.

rules.title: 2. Wish + Past Perfect (Past Regret)
rules.explanation: Use the past perfect for regrets about the past.
rules.structure: wish + subject + had + past participle.
notes: Correct: I wish I had studied harder.
This refers to an action you did not do.

rules.title: 3. Wish + Would (Change Wanted)
rules.explanation: Use 'would' to express a wish for someone to change or for something to happen.
rules.structure: wish / if only + subject + would + base verb.
notes: Correct: If only she would listen to me.
Do not use 'will' after 'if only' in this sense.

common_mistakes.wrong: I wish I have more time.
common_mistakes.correct: I wish I had more time.
common_mistakes.reason: Use the past simple after 'wish' for present unreal wishes.

common_mistakes.wrong: If only he will call me.
common_mistakes.correct: If only he would call me.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Would' is used after 'if only' for wishes about future change.

other_examples.sentence: I wish I were taller.
other_examples.translation: Saya berharap saya lebih tinggi.

explanation.en: 'Were' is used after 'wish' in formal English.
explanation.id: 'Were' digunakan setelah 'wish' dalam bahasa Inggris formal.

other_examples.sentence: If only we had left earlier.
other_examples.translation: Andai saja kami berangkat lebih awal.

explanation.en: 'If only + past perfect' expresses regret about the past.
explanation.id: 'If only + past perfect' mengungkapkan penyesalan atas masa lalu.

other_examples.sentence: I wish it would stop raining.
other_examples.translation: Saya berharap hujan segera berhenti.

explanation.en: 'Wish + would' for a desired change.
explanation.id: 'Wish + would' untuk perubahan yang diinginkan.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: Neither the manager nor his assistants was aware of the changes that had been made to the contract.
tokens: Neither the manager nor his assistants

details_explanation.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Here, the closer subject is 'his assistants' (plural), so the verb should be 'were', not 'was'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the proximity rule with correlative conjunctions. In 'neither A nor B', the verb agrees with B, the nearest subject.

rules.title: 1. The Proximity Rule
rules.explanation: In 'neither X nor Y' and 'either X or Y', the verb agrees with Y.
rules.structure: Neither + plural + nor + singular + singular verb; Neither + singular + nor + plural + plural verb.
notes: Correct: Neither the manager nor his assistants were...
Correct: Neither his assistants nor the manager was...

rules.title: 2. 'Nor' as a Negative
rules.explanation: 'Nor' already carries negation, so do not add another negative later in the sentence.
rules.structure: Neither ... nor + affirmative verb.
notes: Correct: Neither he nor she was ready.
Incorrect: Neither he nor she wasn't ready.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: The nearest noun is 'assistants' (plural), so 'were aware' is correct.
rules.structure: Neither the manager nor his assistants were aware.
notes: Correct answer: 'were aware'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Neither the students nor the teacher were present.
common_mistakes.correct: Neither the students nor the teacher was present.
common_mistakes.reason: The nearer subject 'the teacher' is singular, so use 'was'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Neither of them are coming.
common_mistakes.correct: Neither of them is coming.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Neither of' is treated as singular in formal English.

other_examples.sentence: Neither the driver nor the passengers were injured.
other_examples.translation: Baik pengemudi maupun penumpang tidak terluka.

explanation.en: Plural nearer subject 'passengers' takes 'were'.
explanation.id: Subjek terdekat 'passengers' yang jamak menggunakan 'were'.

other_examples.sentence: Neither the players nor the coach was satisfied.
other_examples.translation: Baik para pemain maupun pelatih tidak puas.

explanation.en: Singular nearer subject 'coach' takes 'was'.
explanation.id: Subjek terdekat 'coach' yang tunggal menggunakan 'was'.

other_examples.sentence: Either my brothers or my sister is picking me up.
other_examples.translation: Entah saudara-saudara lelaki saya atau kakak perempuan saya yang menjemput.

explanation.en: 'Either ... or' also follows the proximity rule.
explanation.id: 'Either ... or' juga mengikuti aturan kedekatan.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: The number of applicants who have applied for the scholarship have risen sharply this year.

details_explanation.explanation: The subject is 'The number', which is singular, so the main verb must be 'has risen'. The plural noun 'applicants' is part of the prepositional phrase and does not control the main verb.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests a classic agreement trap. 'The number of + plural noun' is singular because the head noun is 'number'. In contrast, 'a number of + plural noun' is plural because it means 'several'.

rules.title: 1. 'The Number Of' Is Singular
rules.explanation: The head noun is 'number', so the verb is singular.
rules.structure: The number of + plural noun + singular verb.
notes: Correct: The number of applicants has risen.
Incorrect: The number of applicants have risen.

rules.title: 2. 'A Number Of' Is Plural
rules.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.
rules.structure: A number of + plural noun + plural verb.
notes: Correct: A number of applicants have applied.
The relative clause 'who have applied' correctly agrees with 'applicants'.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: Replace 'have risen' with 'has risen'. The relative clause 'who have applied' is already correct.
rules.structure: The number of applicants who have applied for the scholarship has risen sharply this year.
notes: Correct answer: 'has risen'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The number of students are increasing.
common_mistakes.correct: The number of students is increasing.
common_mistakes.reason: 'The number' is singular.

common_mistakes.wrong: A number of students is absent today.
common_mistakes.correct: A number of students are absent today.
common_mistakes.reason: 'A number of' means 'several' and is plural.

other_examples.sentence: The number of tourists visiting Bali has increased.
other_examples.translation: Jumlah wisatawan yang mengunjungi Bali telah meningkat.

explanation.en: 'The number' takes the singular 'has increased'.
explanation.id: 'The number' menggunakan bentuk tunggal 'has increased'.

other_examples.sentence: A number of issues remain unresolved.
other_examples.translation: Sejumlah masalah masih belum terselesaikan.

explanation.en: 'A number of' takes the plural 'remain'.
explanation.id: 'A number of' menggunakan bentuk jamak 'remain'.

other_examples.sentence: The amount of water in the reservoir is decreasing.
other_examples.translation: Jumlah air di waduk itu menurun.

explanation.en: 'The amount of' with uncountable nouns is singular.
explanation.id: 'The amount of' dengan kata benda tak terhitung bersifat tunggal.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: The supervisor insisted in reviewing every document before it was sent to the client.

details_explanation.explanation: The verb 'insist' is followed by the preposition 'on', not 'in'. The correct phrase is 'insisted on reviewing'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests common verb + preposition combinations that are frequently confused by learners, such as insist on, depend on, rely on, and consist of.

rules.title: 1. Insist On + Noun/Gerund
rules.explanation: 'Insist' is always followed by 'on' (or 'that').
rules.structure: insist on + noun/verb-ing; insist that + clause.
notes: Correct: insisted on reviewing.
Correct: insisted that the document be reviewed.

rules.title: 2. Other Common Collocations
rules.explanation: Learn prepositions as part of the verb.
rules.structure: depend on, rely on, consist of, apologise for, accuse of.
notes: Correct: depends on the weather.
Incorrect: depends of the weather.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: Replace 'insisted in' with 'insisted on'.
rules.structure: The supervisor insisted on reviewing every document...
notes: Correct answer: 'insisted on'.

common_mistakes.wrong: She insisted in paying for the meal.
common_mistakes.correct: She insisted on paying for the meal.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Insist' is followed by 'on'.

common_mistakes.wrong: It depends of your decision.
common_mistakes.correct: It depends on your decision.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Depend' takes 'on'.

other_examples.sentence: He insisted on driving me home.
other_examples.translation: Dia bersikeras mengantar saya pulang.

explanation.en: 'Insist on + gerund'.
explanation.id: 'Insist on + gerund'.

other_examples.sentence: The results depend on several factors.
other_examples.translation: Hasilnya bergantung pada beberapa faktor.

explanation.en: 'Depend on' is the correct collocation.
explanation.id: 'Depend on' adalah kolokasi yang benar.

other_examples.sentence: The committee consists of five members.
other_examples.translation: Komite itu terdiri dari lima anggota.

explanation.en: 'Consist of' is the correct collocation.
explanation.id: 'Consist of' adalah kolokasi yang benar.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: The more carefully you plan, the less mistakes you will make.

details_explanation.explanation: 'Mistakes' is a plural countable noun, so the correct comparative quantifier is 'fewer', not 'less'. 'Less' is used with uncountable nouns.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the double comparative structure 'the more ... the ...' combined with the countable/uncountable distinction between 'fewer' and 'less'.

rules.title: 1. Fewer vs Less
rules.explanation: Use 'fewer' with plural countable nouns and 'less' with uncountable nouns.
rules.structure: fewer + plural noun; less + uncountable noun.
notes: Correct: fewer mistakes.
Correct: less time.
Incorrect: less mistakes.

rules.title: 2. Double Comparative Structure
rules.explanation: Use 'the + comparative ..., the + comparative ...' to show a parallel change.
rules.structure: The more + clause, the fewer/less + clause.
notes: Correct: The more carefully you plan, the fewer mistakes you will make.
Both halves need a comparative.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: Replace 'the less mistakes' with 'the fewer mistakes'.
rules.structure: The more carefully you plan, the fewer mistakes you will make.
notes: Correct answer: 'the fewer mistakes'.

common_mistakes.wrong: There are less students this year.
common_mistakes.correct: There are fewer students this year.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Students' is countable, so use 'fewer'.

common_mistakes.wrong: The more you practise, the more better you become.
common_mistakes.correct: The more you practise, the better you become.
common_mistakes.reason: Do not use 'more' with '-er' comparatives.

other_examples.sentence: The earlier you leave, the less traffic you will meet.
other_examples.translation: Semakin awal kamu berangkat, semakin sedikit kemacetan yang kamu temui.

explanation.en: 'Traffic' is uncountable, so 'less' is correct.
explanation.id: 'Traffic' tidak terhitung, sehingga 'less' benar.

other_examples.sentence: The more books you read, the more knowledge you gain.
other_examples.translation: Semakin banyak buku yang kamu baca, semakin banyak pengetahuan yang kamu peroleh.

explanation.en: Both halves use 'the more' with countable/uncountable nouns.
explanation.id: Kedua bagian menggunakan 'the more' dengan kata benda terhitung/tak terhitung.

other_examples.sentence: The fewer distractions you have, the faster you finish.
other_examples.translation: Semakin sedikit gangguan yang kamu miliki, semakin cepat kamu selesai.

explanation.en: 'Fewer distractions' uses the countable form.
explanation.id: 'Fewer distractions' menggunakan bentuk terhitung.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: Although the heavy rain, the football match continued without interruption.
correctAnswers: In spite of the heavy rain

name.id: Kata Hubung Kontras — Although vs Despite

details_explanation.explanation: 'Although' must be followed by a full clause (subject + verb). A noun phrase like 'the heavy rain' needs 'Despite' or 'In spite of'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests the grammatical difference between concessive linkers. 'Although/even though/though' take clauses; 'despite/in spite of' take noun phrases or gerunds.

rules.title: 1. Although + Clause
rules.explanation: 'Although' introduces a full clause with a subject and finite verb.
rules.structure: Although + subject + verb, main clause.
notes: Correct: Although it was raining heavily, the match continued.
Incorrect: Although the heavy rain...

rules.title: 2. Despite / In Spite Of + Noun
rules.explanation: These linkers are followed by a noun, pronoun, or gerund.
rules.structure: Despite / In spite of + noun phrase, main clause.
notes: Correct: Despite the heavy rain...
Correct: In spite of the heavy rain...

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: Replace 'Although the heavy rain' with 'Despite the heavy rain' or 'In spite of the heavy rain'.
rules.structure: Despite the heavy rain, the football match continued without interruption.
notes: Correct answers: 'Despite the heavy rain' and 'In spite of the heavy rain'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite of the rain, we went out.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the rain, we went out.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Although the bad weather, the event succeeded.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the bad weather, the event succeeded.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Although' needs a clause.

other_examples.sentence: Although he was exhausted, he finished the race.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun dia kelelahan, dia menyelesaikan perlombaan itu.

explanation.en: 'Although' is followed by a full clause.
explanation.id: 'Although' diikuti oleh klausa lengkap.

other_examples.sentence: Despite her injury, she completed the marathon.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun cedera, dia menyelesaikan maraton itu.

explanation.en: 'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase.
explanation.id: 'Despite' diikuti oleh frasa nomina.

other_examples.sentence: In spite of working overtime, he missed the deadline.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun bekerja lembur, dia melewatkan tenggat waktu.

explanation.en: 'In spite of' can be followed by a gerund.
explanation.id: 'In spite of' dapat diikuti gerund.

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and correct it.
questions.sentence: We are looking forward to hear from you soon.

name.id: Kata Kerja Berpreposisi + Gerund — 'look forward to'

details_explanation.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. Therefore, it is followed by a gerund: 'hearing', not 'hear'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests prepositional verbs that end in 'to'. The 'to' is a preposition, so the verb after it takes the -ing form. Common examples are look forward to, be used to, object to, and in addition to.

rules.title: 1. 'To' as a Preposition
rules.explanation: When 'to' is part of a prepositional verb, use a noun or gerund after it.
rules.structure: look forward to + noun/verb-ing.
notes: Correct: looking forward to hearing from you.
Incorrect: looking forward to hear from you.

rules.title: 2. Contrast with Infinitive 'to'
rules.explanation: Some structures use 'to + base verb' (e.g., want to go). The difference depends on the verb.
rules.structure: want to do vs. look forward to doing.
notes: Correct: I want to see you.
Correct: I look forward to seeing you.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rule
rules.explanation: Replace 'hear from you' with 'hearing from you'.
rules.structure: We are looking forward to hearing from you soon.
notes: Correct answer: 'hearing from you'.

common_mistakes.wrong: I object to be treated like this.
common_mistakes.correct: I object to being treated like this.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Object to' is followed by a gerund.

common_mistakes.wrong: She is used to work late.
common_mistakes.correct: She is used to working late.
common_mistakes.reason: 'Be used to' is followed by a gerund.

other_examples.sentence: I look forward to meeting you in person.
other_examples.translation: Saya menantikan bertemu langsung dengan Anda.

explanation.en: 'Look forward to + gerund'.
explanation.id: 'Look forward to + gerund'.

other_examples.sentence: They object to paying extra fees.
other_examples.translation: Mereka menolak membayar biaya tambahan.

explanation.en: 'Object to' takes a gerund.
explanation.id: 'Object to' memerlukan gerund.

other_examples.sentence: In addition to teaching, she writes novels.
other_examples.translation: Selain mengajar, dia juga menulis novel.

explanation.en: 'In addition to' is a prepositional phrase followed by a gerund.
explanation.id: 'In addition to' adalah frasa preposisional yang diikuti gerund.

questions.passage: The Komodo dragon, found only in a few Indonesian islands, is the world's largest living lizard. Despite its size, it can run surprisingly fast over short distances. Its bite is venomous, and recent research has shown that the venom, rather than bacteria, is primarily responsible for the severity of its victims' wounds. Conservation efforts are complicated by the fact that the species is vulnerable to habitat loss and, in some areas, to a shrinking prey base.
questions.question: Which TWO statements are supported by the passage?

options.A: The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard in the world.
options.C: Recent research suggests that venom plays a major role in the severity of wounds.
options.D: Conservation is easy because the species is widespread.

name.id: Pemahaman Bacaan — Beberapa Pernyataan yang Didukung

details_explanation.explanation: A restates 'the world's largest living lizard'. C restates 'recent research has shown that the venom ... is primarily responsible for the severity of its victims' wounds'. B contradicts 'can run surprisingly fast', and D contradicts 'Conservation efforts are complicated'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question asks you to identify two statements that are directly supported by the passage. Multiple-answer reading questions require checking each option against the text separately.

rules.title: 1. Check Each Option Against the Text
rules.explanation: Do not choose an option simply because it sounds plausible; find the exact supporting phrase.
rules.structure: Option → matching phrase in passage.
notes: A → 'the world's largest living lizard'.
C → 'the venom ... is primarily responsible for the severity'.

rules.title: 2. Reject Contradictions
rules.explanation: If an option contradicts the passage, it is definitely wrong.
rules.structure: Passage says X; option says not-X → wrong.
notes: B contradicts 'can run surprisingly fast'.
D contradicts 'Conservation efforts are complicated'.

rules.title: 3. Watch for Qualifiers
rules.explanation: Words like 'primarily', 'some', and 'only' are important and often tested.
rules.structure: Match qualifiers exactly.
notes: Correct answers: A and C.
The passage says 'primarily responsible', not 'solely responsible'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Choosing an option because it is generally true about the animal.
common_mistakes.correct: Choose only options with direct textual support.
common_mistakes.reason: Reading comprehension answers must come from the passage.

common_mistakes.wrong: Choosing one correct answer and stopping.
common_mistakes.correct: Check every option because the question asks for TWO.
common_mistakes.reason: Multiple-answer questions require checking all options.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: The museum closes at 5 p.m., but the café remains open until 8 p.m. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Museum tutup pukul 5 sore, tetapi kafenya buka sampai pukul 8 malam. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

explanation.en: Supported: the museum closes at 5 p.m.; the café opens later than the museum.
explanation.id: Didukung: museum tutup pukul 5 sore; kafe tutup lebih lambat.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: Sales rose in Asia but fell in Europe. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Penjualan naik di Asia tetapi turun di Eropa. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

explanation.en: Supported: Asian sales increased; European sales decreased.
explanation.id: Didukung: penjualan Asia meningkat; penjualan Eropa menurun.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: The study included 200 adults and 100 children. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Studi itu melibatkan 200 orang dewasa dan 100 anak. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

explanation.en: Supported: there were more adults than children; the total was 300.
explanation.id: Didukung: jumlah orang dewasa lebih banyak; totalnya 300.

questions.passage: The Borobudur temple, built in the ninth century, is the world's largest Buddhist temple. It was abandoned for centuries after the decline of Buddhism in Java and was rediscovered in the early nineteenth century. Today it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and restoration work continues to protect the structure from erosion and volcanic ash.
questions.question: Which TWO statements are supported by the passage?

options.A: Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world.
options.B: Borobudur was built in the tenth century.
options.C: The temple was abandoned for several centuries.

name.id: Pemahaman Bacaan — Beberapa Pernyataan yang Didukung

details_explanation.explanation: A matches 'the world's largest Buddhist temple'. C matches 'abandoned for centuries'. B contradicts 'built in the ninth century', and D contradicts 'restoration work continues'.
details_explanation.introduction: This question tests careful reading of factual details and dates. Pay attention to exact numbers and the tense of ongoing actions.

rules.title: 1. Match Dates Precisely
rules.explanation: The passage says 'ninth century', not 'tenth century'.
rules.structure: ninth century → option B is false.
notes: Small numeric differences make an option wrong.

rules.title: 2. Check the Tense of Ongoing Actions
rules.explanation: 'Restoration work continues' means it is still happening, so 'has been completed' is false.
rules.structure: continues ≠ completed.
notes: Option D is contradicted by the present tense 'continues'.

rules.title: 3. Confirm Both Correct Options
rules.explanation: A and C are both directly stated.
rules.structure: Correct answers: A and C.
notes: Always locate the exact supporting sentence.

common_mistakes.wrong: Assuming restoration is finished because the site is a World Heritage Site.
common_mistakes.correct: The passage says restoration 'continues'.
common_mistakes.reason: Do not infer beyond the text.

common_mistakes.wrong: Mixing up 'ninth' and 'tenth'.
common_mistakes.correct: The passage says 'ninth century'.
common_mistakes.reason: Read numbers carefully.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: The bridge was completed in 1998 and repaired in 2015. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Jembatan itu selesai pada 1998 dan diperbaiki pada 2015. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

explanation.en: Supported: the bridge is older than the repair; it was repaired in 2015.
explanation.id: Didukung: jembatan lebih tua daripada perbaikannya; diperbaiki pada 2015.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: The course lasts six weeks and includes weekly quizzes. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Kursus berlangsung enam minggu dan mencakup kuis mingguan. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

explanation.en: Supported: the course lasts six weeks; there is more than one quiz.
explanation.id: Didukung: kursus berlangsung enam minggu; ada lebih dari satu kuis.

other_examples.sentence: Passage: The factory employs 500 workers, most of whom commute by bus. Question: Which TWO statements are supported?
other_examples.translation: Bacaan: Pabrik itu mempekerjakan 500 pekerja, sebagian besar dari mereka bepergian dengan bus. Pertanyaan: Dua pernyataan mana yang didukung?

details_explanation.introduction: This question tests two agreement patterns in one sentence: a relative clause must agree with its antecedent, and a collective noun such as 'committee', 'team', or 'government' usually takes a singular verb when acting as one body.

rules.title: 1. Relative Clause Agreement
rules.explanation: 'That/who/which' takes its verb agreement from the noun it refers to.
rules.structure: noun (plural) + that + plural verb.

rules.title: 2. Collective Nouns
rules.explanation: Words like committee, team, board, and government are usually singular when they act as one unit.

rules.title: 3. Applying the Rules

notes: Correct answer: 'Despite'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite of the fact that he was ill, he attended.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the fact that he was ill, he attended. / In spite of the fact that he was ill, he attended.
common_mistakes.reason: Never write 'despite of'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Despite the fact he was ill, he attended.
common_mistakes.correct: Despite the fact that he was ill, he attended.
common_mistakes.reason: Keep 'that' in the fixed phrase.

other_examples.sentence: Despite the fact that she was exhausted, she finished the race.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun dia kelelahan, dia menyelesaikan perlombaan itu.

explanation.en: 'Despite the fact that' introduces a full clause.
explanation.id: 'Despite the fact that' memperkenalkan klausa lengkap.

other_examples.sentence: In spite of the fact that prices had risen, sales increased.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun harga naik, penjualan meningkat.

explanation.en: 'In spite of the fact that' is also correct.
explanation.id: 'In spite of the fact that' juga benar.

other_examples.sentence: Despite the delay, the passengers remained calm.
other_examples.translation: Meskipun ada penundaan, para penumpang tetap tenang.

explanation.en: 'Despite + noun phrase' is the shorter form.
explanation.id: 'Despite + frasa nomina' adalah bentuk yang lebih pendek.
